newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel budget gap 1.28 billion shekel in January.
newsitem.headline: Israel budget gap 1.28 billion shekel in January.

text.p: Israel recorded a budget deficit of 1.283 billion shekels in January, preliminary figures released by the Treasury on Sunday showed.
Note: Figures are in millions of shekels.

Treasury officials noted that the figure included both the domestic and foreign deficit. The domestic deficit, which until now was the sole figure published on a monthly basis, was 1.146 billion shekels, it added.

The ministry said the deficit was raised by seasonal payments made to the health maintenance organisations. It said tax revenues had shown a slight increase for the month but remained at the low levels that characterised 1996.
The budget calls for a full-year deficit of 9.744 billion shekels.

The Treasury for the first time also provided figures on how the deficit was financed. For January, it said it raised 1.01 billion shekels in the domestic capital market and drew down 623 million shekels in deposits with the central bank. Overseas, it paid back a net 454 million shekels in foreign debt.
